Class 3 · Chapter 10 of 10

Codes, positions and picture puzzles

Use codes and clues, find ranks and ways to choose, and follow directions.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Number, letter and picture patterns. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can use a code or word clue.
  • I can find ranks and allowed combinations.
  • I can find a hidden letter and follow directions.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Letter codes

In this code each letter moves one step forward. A becomes B.

So CAT becomes DBU. To decode, move each letter one step back.

Screen 2 of 5

Ranks in a queue

Asha is 4th from the front in a queue of 9.

There are 3 people in front of her and 5 behind her.

Screen 3 of 5

Ways to choose

2 tops and 3 bottoms: every top can go with every bottom.

2 × 3 = 6 different outfits.

Screen 4 of 5

Find a hidden letter

A letter can hide inside a bigger picture.

Find the exact shape, same size and same way up. Here an L hides in the corner.

Screen 5 of 5

Follow directions

Go East, East, North, North on this board. North is up.

The otter goes round the wall and reaches the goal.

Words to know
code
A secret way of writing, such as moving every letter one step forward.
rank
A place in order, like 3rd from the front.
compass directions
North, East, South and West. Up is North.

For parents

What your child learns

Logic puzzles use order, turns and rules. If a row is turned round, left and right swap. On a grid, north is up, east is right, and each step moves one square.

A common slip

Children often forget a move or mix up left and right after a turn. Draw the path and mark each move. Check each clue again with the final answer.

5-minute home activity: Grid walk

  1. Draw a 4 by 4 grid and label the columns A to D.
  2. Put a counter on a start square.
  3. Give moves such as north 2, east 1 and west 2.
  4. Say which square you reach and check by moving it.
